whyThisMatters:
BoomCloud helps a dental practice sell patients a membership, so the clinic is not only living on insurance reimbursements. The founder came from a family dental lab. He says the company has been profitable since 2016, and that there was no outside funding in the episode.

About three million a year. About six hundred practices. Eleven people. January 2026. Self-reported. Dentistry is a slow trade. A membership is recurring cash for the clinic, and the software is how they run it.

You pay so the patient is on a plan the clinic owns.

Eleven people and about six hundred practices is a small team for a national dental tool. Profitable since 2016 is his line, and the episode does not mention a funding round. Insurance reimbursement is the thing the membership is meant to sit beside, not a number I am adding.

The family dental lab is the background, not a second product. Membership revenue for the clinic is the change he is selling. Conservative buyers are why he says a small bootstrapped team beats a land grab.
